notes: Paper presents constraints on ultralight dark matter (ULDM) couplings to fundamental constants using atomic clock comparisons (87Sr, 171Yb+, 133Cs). Primary new limits are on scalar field couplings d(n)_gamma, d(n)_me, d(n)_g, and d(n)_q. Figure 6 (top panel) shows constraints on linear photon coupling d(1)_gamma vs axion mass m_phi, with best-fit Yb+/Sr data (red line) and 95% C.L. (light red band). Data points extracted from Fig. 6 top panel showing approximate exclusion boundary. The paper uses a model-independent effective field theory framework to describe time variations of fundamental constants via coupling to a scalar field phi(t). For ULDM interpretation, assumes Standard Halo Model with local DM density rho_DM ≈ 0.3 GeV/cm³. Constraints span mass range ~10^-20 to 10^-17 eV. Paper claims order-of-magnitude improvement over previous Rb/Cs clock studies in this mass range due to larger sensitivity coefficient |ΔK_Yb+/Sr_alpha| ≈ 6 vs |ΔK_Rb/Cs_alpha| ≈ 0.5. Also provides constraints on quadratic couplings d(2)_gamma and other scalar couplings (d_me, d_g, d_q, Higgs coupling A). Oscillatory analysis uses Lomb-Scargle periodogram on ~2 week atomic clock data from July 2019 at NPL. | selector: figure (sole candidate)
